transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… mostly I just don’t feel like myself anymore. It’s hard to explain without sounding lazy or dramatic, but I used to be pretty active. I’d go hiking whenever I could, I coached, I played guitar, I used to call people back and keep up with folks. And now I just… don’t.

It’s not even always that I decide not to. It’s more like everything takes this huge amount of effort I can’t seem to get started on. I’ll sit in my little rental place for hours, knowing there are things I should do — basic things, stuff I used to just handle — and I just sit there. I know I should move, make a call, pick up the guitar, go outside, something, but it’s like the part of me that starts things isn’t working right.

That’s really why I’m here. I feel like I’ve kind of disappeared from my own life.
Did this start after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Yeah… I mean, the big thing was the divorce and moving out. I moved into this smaller rental place afterward, and I think that’s when things really started to come apart. It wasn’t like one day everything snapped, exactly, but since then it’s been… unraveling.

That was about a year and two months ago now, give or take. And at first I thought, okay, anyone would feel thrown off after a divorce, after packing up your life and ending up in a place that doesn’t feel like yours. I kept telling myself I’d settle in, get my routines back, make the place feel normal. But instead it just kept stretching on, and I kept getting further away from how I used to be.
For most of the time over the past year, have you felt down or unable to enjoy things nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d call it “down” every day exactly… not like crying all the time or anything. It’s more that I don’t feel like myself. Most days I just don’t get any enjoyment out of the things I used to actually care about.

I used to hike a lot, and I coached, and I’d play guitar just because it felt good to play. I used to call people back, check in, keep up with plans. Now all of that feels like it belongs to somebody else. Some days I sit in that small rental for hours, and I know there are things I should be doing — even simple things — but I can’t make myself start. I’ll think, “Get up, go outside, pick up the guitar, call someone,” and then I just… don’t.

So yeah, most of the time over the past year, it’s been like that. Not exactly sadness every minute, but the enjoyment and motivation are mostly gone.
Since this started, have there been stretches of at least two months when you felt mostly back to your usual self?

No… I don’t think so. Not for two months, definitely not.

There might have been a day here or there where I thought, okay, maybe I’m getting a little more normal, or I got something done and felt like maybe I was turning a corner. But then it would go right back to the same thing. Since I moved into that smaller rental after the divorce — and that’s been about a year and two months now — it’s felt like things have just kept unraveling.

I kept expecting there to be a stretch where I’d settle in and feel like myself again, but that stretch never really came.
Over the past year, have you felt sad or depressed most of the day on most days?

I’m not sure I’d say sad or depressed most of the day, most days. That’s the part I have trouble answering cleanly.

There are definitely days where I feel low, or heavy, like everything is gray, but I don’t know if it’s “sad” exactly. It’s not always like I’m sitting there thinking, “I’m depressed.” Sometimes it’s more blank than sad, if that makes sense. Like I’m just moving through the day and everything feels muted.

So… I guess I can’t honestly say I’ve felt sad most of the day on most days. I’ve felt off, and not myself, and kind of weighed down a lot of the time, but the word sad doesn’t always fit.
Over the past six months, have you been worrying excessively about a number of different things?

I don’t know… “excessively” is hard for me to judge.

I worry about things, sure, like anybody would, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s been a bunch of different things all the time. Sometimes my mind gets stuck on something and I’ll go over it too much, but when you say worrying excessively about a number of different things, I’m not sure that fits exactly.

Can you say what you mean by “excessively”? Like, do you mean not being able to control it, or worrying about everyday stuff more than makes sense? Because I’m not sure I’ve noticed it that way.
Do these symptoms feel stronger than you’d expect from the divorce and move alone?

I don’t know how to measure that, honestly.

I mean, the divorce and the move were big. They weren’t small things. It changed my whole routine, where I was living, what I came home to, how I thought my life was supposed to look. So part of me thinks, well, of course I wouldn’t feel normal after that.

But then when you ask “stronger than you’d expect,” I get stuck, because I don’t really know what the expected amount is. I keep comparing it to what I think other people might go through, or what I would’ve told someone else in my job to push through, but that doesn’t really answer it.

It feels like more than I know how to explain sometimes, but I also don’t want to make it sound like the divorce and move weren’t enough to affect me. So… I’m not sure. I guess I can say it hasn’t felt like I bounced back the way I thought I would, but whether that means it’s stronger than expected, I don’t know.
During this past year, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I can say yes to that in a clean way.

There have been stretches where I felt really low and like I was underwater, I guess, but “depressed most of the day nearly every day for two weeks” is hard for me to pin down. I don’t track it that neatly. Some days I wake up feeling heavy, and then later I’m more numb than sad, or I’m distracted for a while, and then it comes back. So I don’t know if that counts as depressed most of the day.

If you mean was there a clear two-week block where I was sad all day, every day, then… I don’t know. I don’t think I can confidently say that. It’s been more uneven than that, or maybe I’m just bad at remembering it in the way you’re asking.
Over the past year, have there been more days than not when you felt down, low, or hopeless?

I’m not sure. “More days than not” is the part I get stuck on, because I don’t think I’ve been keeping count in a way where I can say yes or no.

There have been plenty of days where I felt low, or flat, or like things were kind of pointless, but then I’ll have days where I’m functioning or distracted enough that I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless. And sometimes it’s not exactly sadness, it’s more like this heavy feeling, or like I’m just going through motions, and I don’t know whether that counts as “down.”

If you’re asking whether it’s been a constant thing most of the year, I can’t honestly say I know. It feels like it’s been around a lot, but I don’t want to guess and tell you it was more than half the days if I’m not sure.
Over this past year, have you had a noticeable change in your sleep?

I’m not sure how to answer that clearly. I mean, my sleep hasn’t felt great, but I don’t know if I’d call it a noticeable change in the way you’re asking.

Some nights I sleep, some nights I don’t feel like I slept well, but I haven’t been keeping track of hours or anything. It’s not like I can point to a specific point and say, “That’s when my sleep changed.” With everything that’s happened, my routine has been off in general, so it’s hard to separate whether my sleep itself changed or whether my whole life just got less regular.

I guess what I can say is I don’t wake up feeling especially rested a lot of the time, but I don’t know if that’s new-new, or if I’m just paying more attention to it now. So… maybe? But I wouldn’t want to overstate it.
In this past year, was there ever a period when you felt down or empty nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I know you’re asking it a little differently, but I still don’t really know how to give a definite yes.

There have been times where I felt empty, definitely, like not much was reaching me, and it would go on for a while. But whether it was nearly every day for two straight weeks… I can’t say for sure. My memory of it doesn’t line up into neat blocks like that. Some days I’d feel low for a big part of the day, and then other times I’d just feel blank, or I’d get through work or whatever I had to do and not really register how I felt until later.

So if you mean, “Can I point to a specific two-week stretch where almost every day I felt down or empty?” I can’t honestly point to one and say yes. It’s more like it comes in waves, or it’s in the background, but I’m not confident about the timing.
Do you feel that your problems began only after the divorce and move?

I wouldn’t say only after the divorce and move, exactly, but that’s when it really started feeling like things were unraveling. After I moved into the smaller rental, after the divorce, everything just felt… reduced, I guess. Smaller place, different routine, different sense of myself.

That was about a year and two months ago. I remember it because it wasn’t just a change of address, it felt like this line where before that I was holding things together better, or at least I thought I was. And then after the move, things started slipping in a way I couldn’t really explain neatly.

So if you’re asking when it became noticeable to me, I’d point to that time — moving into that rental after the divorce. But I don’t know if I can say the problems began only then, like nothing was there before. It’s more that that’s when it all started coming apart.
Before the divorce and move, were you already having this same loss of interest and trouble getting yourself to do things?

Before? Not in the same way, no. I mean, I had normal times where I’d be tired or put things off, like anybody, but I still felt like me. I still had things I did without having to argue with myself for an hour first.

I used to hike pretty regularly. I was coaching, I played guitar, I’d call people back when they called me. Maybe not instantly, but I wasn’t just ignoring everything. Those things felt connected to who I was. Now it’s more like… I know those things exist, and I know I used to care about them, but I can’t really reach that feeling.

Since being in the rental, especially, I’ll sit there for hours knowing there are things I need to do — dishes, laundry, bills, returning a message, even just getting up and going outside — and I just don’t start. It’s not exactly laziness. I know how that sounds, but it doesn’t feel like choosing not to do it. It feels like the part of me that used to get moving just isn’t there.

So before the divorce and the move, maybe there were little signs or maybe I’m remembering it wrong, but it wasn’t this same loss of interest. It wasn’t this feeling that my whole life got smaller and I just stopped doing the things that made me feel like myself.
Over the past year, have you had a noticeable change in your appetite?

I’m not sure I’d call it noticeable. I mean, I haven’t really tracked it closely. Some days I eat like normal, and other days I sort of forget or I just eat whatever’s easiest, but I don’t know if that’s a real appetite change or just how my days go.

I haven’t had a clear thing where I’m suddenly starving all the time or where food is disgusting to me every day. If there’s been a change, it’s not one I can confidently point to. I don’t weigh myself much either, so I can’t really use that as proof of anything.
Over the past year, have you had low energy nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, “energy” is a little hard for me to separate from everything else, but most days I don’t feel like myself anymore. It’s not just being tired like after a long shift or a bad night’s sleep. It’s more like I don’t have the push in me.

I used to be a person who did things. I hiked, I coached, I played guitar, I’d call people back. Those weren’t huge heroic things, they were just… part of me. And now I’ll be sitting in that small rental, looking around at things I know need doing, and I can sit there for hours. I’ll know the laundry needs to be moved, or that I should get up and go outside, or answer someone’s message, and it’s like I can’t get myself started.

So if that counts as low energy, then yes, it’s been there a lot. Nearly every day, probably. It’s not always that I feel physically exhausted exactly. Sometimes it’s more like the part that starts the engine is missing.
Over the past year, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’m sure there are times I don’t focus great, but I don’t know if it’s a symptom or just… life being messy.

Like, with decisions, I can still make them if I really have to. If something is urgent or someone is standing there waiting on me, I usually pick something and move. But when it’s more open-ended, like deciding what to do first at home or what I should take care of on a day off, I can get stuck. I’ll go back and forth over small things longer than makes sense. But I don’t know if that’s “trouble making decisions” in the way you mean.

Concentration is kind of similar. Sometimes I read the same thing a few times or I lose the thread of what I was doing, but I haven’t been keeping track of it. It’s not like I can point to one big obvious change and say, yes, this started then and it’s been happening every day. It’s more that some days my head feels crowded or slow, and other days it’s not as bad.

So… maybe a little, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s been a clear, noticeable problem over the whole past year.
Over the past year, have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

I… I don’t know. That’s a hard one to answer straight.

I don’t think I walk around thinking that exact sentence, like, “life isn’t worth living,” all day or anything. But there are definitely times where I feel worn down enough that I think, what is the point of all this, you know? Like I’m just getting through the day and then there’s another day after that, and I don’t have a good answer for what I’m doing it for.

But I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I’m not sitting there making some clear judgment about life, like a philosophy thing. It’s more like… when I’m alone and everything feels heavy, I can get this feeling that it wouldn’t matter much if I wasn’t around. And then I’ll sort of back away from that thought because it scares me, or because I don’t want to make too much out of it.

So… yes, maybe sometimes. I’m not sure how often counts. It’s not something I’m proud to say, and I haven’t really talked about it much.
At any point in the past year, was there a clear two-week stretch when things got noticeably worse than your usual level?

I’m not sure I can pin it down that neatly, honestly.

I can tell you there have been bad stretches, but whether there was a clear two-week block where I could say, “That was definitely worse than my baseline,” I don’t know. My sense of time has gotten kind of muddy with this stuff. Days run into each other, and then I look back and I’m not sure if something was a few days or a few weeks, or if I’m just remembering the worst parts more strongly.

If you mean, was there a period where everything dipped sharply and stayed that way every day for two weeks straight… I don’t know that I noticed it in that clean of a way. It’s been more uneven, I think. Some days I’ll feel like I’m really dragging, and then another day I can function enough that I tell myself maybe it’s fine, and then it comes back again. So I don’t want to say yes if I’m just guessing.

I’d probably need to look at a calendar or think through what was happening around that time. Off the top of my head, I can’t give you a clear two-week stretch.
Have you had this kind of low or empty mood on most days for at least two years?

I’m not sure I can say that, no. I mean… two years is a long time to look back on and describe accurately. I’ve definitely had low or empty periods, but “most days for at least two years” sounds very specific, and I don’t know that I’ve been tracking it in a way where I could honestly say yes.

Some days I feel kind of flat or like I’m just moving through the motions, and other days it’s not as obvious. Sometimes I only realize I’ve been low after the fact, when someone asks or when I notice I haven’t really felt much of anything for a while. But I can’t tell if that’s been most days, consistently, for two years.

So I guess my answer is… I don’t know. I wouldn’t want to say yes just because it’s been around on and off. If you mean a steady low mood almost every day for two full years, I’m not sure I have that clearly in my head.
If the divorce and move had not happened, do you think you would still be having these problems?

I honestly don’t know how to separate it out that cleanly.

I mean, the divorce and the move were huge, and I’d be lying if I said they didn’t shake things up. They changed my routine, where I was sleeping, who I was around, how I saw myself day to day… all of that. So part of me wants to say, maybe if those things hadn’t happened, maybe I’d be steadier, or maybe I’d have had something familiar to hold onto.

But at the same time, I can’t say with confidence that everything would be fine if they hadn’t happened. That feels too simple. There were things in me that didn’t feel right even before, or at least I think there were, but then when big life stuff happens it gets hard to tell what’s causing what. Like, am I reacting to what happened, or was this already there and the divorce and move just made it harder to ignore? I don’t know.

So… I guess my answer is maybe. Maybe not as bad, maybe different. But I can’t honestly say, “No, I wouldn’t be having these problems.” I just don’t know.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a clear major depressive episode by testing for a core neurovegetative symptom, which best separates major depression from persistent depressive disorder or adjustment disorder given the patient's vague mood description.
doctor.question: Over this past year, have you had a noticeable change in your sleep?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is specifically about changes in sleep over the past year, but the provided symptom profile does not include a sleep-related item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure how to answer that clearly. I mean, my sleep hasn’t felt great, but I don’t know if I’d call it a noticeable change in the way you’re asking.

Some nights I sleep, some nights I don’t feel like I slept well, but I haven’t been keeping track of hours or anything. It’s not like I can point to a specific point and say, “That’s when my sleep changed.” With everything that’s happened, my routine has been off in general, so it’s hard to separate whether my sleep itself changed or whether my whole life just got less regular.

I guess what I can say is I don’t wake up feeling especially rested a lot of the time, but I don’t know if that’s new-new, or if I’m just paying more attention to it now. So… maybe? But I wouldn’t want to overstate it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a sustained period of depressed mood, which best distinguishes a major depressive episode or persistent depressive disorder from adjustment disorder in this ambiguous presentation.
doctor.question: In this past year, was there ever a period when you felt down or empty nearly every day for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a possible depressive episode, specifically feeling down or empty nearly every day for at least two weeks, which is not covered by the listed schizophrenia symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I know you’re asking it a little differently, but I still don’t really know how to give a definite yes.

There have been times where I felt empty, definitely, like not much was reaching me, and it would go on for a while. But whether it was nearly every day for two straight weeks… I can’t say for sure. My memory of it doesn’t line up into neat blocks like that. Some days I’d feel low for a big part of the day, and then other times I’d just feel blank, or I’d get through work or whatever I had to do and not really register how I felt until later.

So if you mean, “Can I point to a specific two-week stretch where almost every day I felt down or empty?” I can’t honestly point to one and say yes. It’s more like it comes in waves, or it’s in the background, but I’m not confident about the timing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's symptoms are confined to a maladaptive response to the divorce/move, which would support adjustment disorder over primary depressive disorders.
doctor.question: Do you feel that your problems began only after the divorce and move?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: Things have been unraveling since I moved into the smaller rental after my divorce, about a year and two months ago.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about when the problems began in relation to the divorce and move, which matches the duration/onset information.

patient.answer:
I wouldn’t say only after the divorce and move, exactly, but that’s when it really started feeling like things were unraveling. After I moved into the smaller rental, after the divorce, everything just felt… reduced, I guess. Smaller place, different routine, different sense of myself.

That was about a year and two months ago. I remember it because it wasn’t just a change of address, it felt like this line where before that I was holding things together better, or at least I thought I was. And then after the move, things started slipping in a way I couldn’t really explain neatly.

So if you’re asking when it became noticeable to me, I’d point to that time — moving into that rental after the divorce. But I don’t know if I can say the problems began only then, like nothing was there before. It’s more that that’s when it all started coming apart.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms are better explained as an adjustment disorder by clarifying whether they were already present before the divorce and move.
doctor.question: Before the divorce and move, were you already having this same loss of interest and trouble getting yourself to do things?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore—I stopped hiking, coaching, playing guitar, and calling people back, and some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things to do but I can't make myself start.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about loss of interest and difficulty initiating activities, which directly matches the negative symptoms profile.

patient.answer:
Before? Not in the same way, no. I mean, I had normal times where I’d be tired or put things off, like anybody, but I still felt like me. I still had things I did without having to argue with myself for an hour first.

I used to hike pretty regularly. I was coaching, I played guitar, I’d call people back when they called me. Maybe not instantly, but I wasn’t just ignoring everything. Those things felt connected to who I was. Now it’s more like… I know those things exist, and I know I used to care about them, but I can’t really reach that feeling.

Since being in the rental, especially, I’ll sit there for hours knowing there are things I need to do — dishes, laundry, bills, returning a message, even just getting up and going outside — and I just don’t start. It’s not exactly laziness. I know how that sounds, but it doesn’t feel like choosing not to do it. It feels like the part of me that used to get moving just isn’t there.

So before the divorce and the move, maybe there were little signs or maybe I’m remembering it wrong, but it wasn’t this same loss of interest. It wasn’t this feeling that my whole life got smaller and I just stopped doing the things that made me feel like myself.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has a key vegetative symptom of a major depressive episode to distinguish major depressive disorder from adjustment disorder or persistent depressive disorder.

I’m not sure I’d call it noticeable. I mean, I haven’t really tracked it closely. Some days I eat like normal, and other days I sort of forget or I just eat whatever’s easiest, but I don’t know if that’s a real appetite change or just how my days go.

I haven’t had a clear thing where I’m suddenly starving all the time or where food is disgusting to me every day. If there’s been a change, it’s not one I can confidently point to. I don’t weigh myself much either, so I can’t really use that as proof of anything.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a clear major depressive symptom outside of subjective mood by assessing fatigue/low energy, which helps distinguish a depressive episode or persistent depressive disorder from adjustment disorder when sadness is unclear.
doctor.question: Over the past year, have you had low energy nearly every day?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: Mostly I just don't feel like myself anymore—I stopped hiking, coaching, playing guitar, and calling people back, and some days I sit in that small rental for hours knowing there are things to do but I can't make myself start.
target_item.reason: The question is about low energy nearly every day over the past year, which most closely relates to diminished motivation and reduced ability to initiate activities described in the negative symptoms profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. I mean, “energy” is a little hard for me to separate from everything else, but most days I don’t feel like myself anymore. It’s not just being tired like after a long shift or a bad night’s sleep. It’s more like I don’t have the push in me.

I used to be a person who did things. I hiked, I coached, I played guitar, I’d call people back. Those weren’t huge heroic things, they were just… part of me. And now I’ll be sitting in that small rental, looking around at things I know need doing, and I can sit there for hours. I’ll know the laundry needs to be moved, or that I should get up and go outside, or answer someone’s message, and it’s like I can’t get myself started.

So if that counts as low energy, then yes, it’s been there a lot. Nearly every day, probably. It’s not always that I feel physically exhausted exactly. Sometimes it’s more like the part that starts the engine is missing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has impaired concentration/indecisiveness, which would help establish whether criteria for a major depressive episode are met and distinguish major depression from adjustment disorder or persistent depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Over the past year, have you had trouble concentrating or making decisions?

target_item.reason: The question is directly about trouble concentrating or making decisions, which is not specifically covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’m sure there are times I don’t focus great, but I don’t know if it’s a symptom or just… life being messy.

Like, with decisions, I can still make them if I really have to. If something is urgent or someone is standing there waiting on me, I usually pick something and move. But when it’s more open-ended, like deciding what to do first at home or what I should take care of on a day off, I can get stuck. I’ll go back and forth over small things longer than makes sense. But I don’t know if that’s “trouble making decisions” in the way you mean.

Concentration is kind of similar. Sometimes I read the same thing a few times or I lose the thread of what I was doing, but I haven’t been keeping track of it. It’s not like I can point to one big obvious change and say, yes, this started then and it’s been happening every day. It’s more that some days my head feels crowded or slow, and other days it’s not as bad.

So… maybe a little, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s been a clear, noticeable problem over the whole past year.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had suicidal thoughts, which would support a major depressive episode and assess safety urgently.
doctor.question: Over the past year, have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal ideation or thoughts that life is not worth living, which is not covered by any item in the provided symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I… I don’t know. That’s a hard one to answer straight.

I don’t think I walk around thinking that exact sentence, like, “life isn’t worth living,” all day or anything. But there are definitely times where I feel worn down enough that I think, what is the point of all this, you know? Like I’m just getting through the day and then there’s another day after that, and I don’t have a good answer for what I’m doing it for.

But I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I’m not sitting there making some clear judgment about life, like a philosophy thing. It’s more like… when I’m alone and everything feels heavy, I can get this feeling that it wouldn’t matter much if I wasn’t around. And then I’ll sort of back away from that thought because it scares me, or because I don’t want to make too much out of it.

So… yes, maybe sometimes. I’m not sure how often counts. It’s not something I’m proud to say, and I haven’t really talked about it much.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was ever a clear 2-week period of markedly increased symptoms to distinguish a major depressive episode from persistent/adaptive depressive symptoms.

target_item.reason: The question is asking about whether there was a distinct two-week period of worsening, likely to assess an episodic mood pattern, but the provided symptom profile only covers overall duration and symptom manifestations, not a clear two-week worsening stretch.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can pin it down that neatly, honestly.

I can tell you there have been bad stretches, but whether there was a clear two-week block where I could say, “That was definitely worse than my baseline,” I don’t know. My sense of time has gotten kind of muddy with this stuff. Days run into each other, and then I look back and I’m not sure if something was a few days or a few weeks, or if I’m just remembering the worst parts more strongly.

If you mean, was there a period where everything dipped sharply and stayed that way every day for two weeks straight… I don’t know that I noticed it in that clean of a way. It’s been more uneven, I think. Some days I’ll feel like I’m really dragging, and then another day I can function enough that I tell myself maybe it’s fine, and then it comes back again. So I don’t want to say yes if I’m just guessing.

I’d probably need to look at a calendar or think through what was happening around that time. Off the top of my head, I can’t give you a clear two-week stretch.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had depressed mood most days for at least two years, which would support persistent depressive disorder over adjustment disorder or a major depressive disorder course.
doctor.question: Have you had this kind of low or empty mood on most days for at least two years?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about chronic low or empty mood for at least two years, which is not covered by the listed schizophrenia symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I can say that, no. I mean… two years is a long time to look back on and describe accurately. I’ve definitely had low or empty periods, but “most days for at least two years” sounds very specific, and I don’t know that I’ve been tracking it in a way where I could honestly say yes.

Some days I feel kind of flat or like I’m just moving through the motions, and other days it’s not as obvious. Sometimes I only realize I’ve been low after the fact, when someone asks or when I notice I haven’t really felt much of anything for a while. But I can’t tell if that’s been most days, consistently, for two years.

So I guess my answer is… I don’t know. I wouldn’t want to say yes just because it’s been around on and off. If you mean a steady low mood almost every day for two full years, I’m not sure I have that clearly in my head.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms are tied specifically to the identifiable stressor, which would help distinguish adjustment disorder from a depressive disorder.
doctor.question: If the divorce and move had not happened, do you think you would still be having these problems?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about whether the divorce and move caused or contributed to the problems, but the symptom profile only covers symptoms, impairment, and duration—not causal attribution.

patient.answer:
I honestly don’t know how to separate it out that cleanly.

I mean, the divorce and the move were huge, and I’d be lying if I said they didn’t shake things up. They changed my routine, where I was sleeping, who I was around, how I saw myself day to day… all of that. So part of me wants to say, maybe if those things hadn’t happened, maybe I’d be steadier, or maybe I’d have had something familiar to hold onto.

But at the same time, I can’t say with confidence that everything would be fine if they hadn’t happened. That feels too simple. There were things in me that didn’t feel right even before, or at least I think there were, but then when big life stuff happens it gets hard to tell what’s causing what. Like, am I reacting to what happened, or was this already there and the divorce and move just made it harder to ignore? I don’t know.

So… I guess my answer is maybe. Maybe not as bad, maybe different. But I can’t honestly say, “No, I wouldn’t be having these problems.” I just don’t know.
